messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD-9283: edge-lb-targets-unhealthy (auto-escalate in 5m). Summary: sudden spike in TLS handshake failures and target health flips for eu-west-1 fronted ALBs. Impact: ~5% increased 5xx for EU customers. Links: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/PD-9283 :rotating_light:

Alex (on-call): ack’ing. I'm taking ownership. Pulling up dashboards + ALB target health. Oncall running `kubectl` checks next.

Maya: seeing handshake failures in the TLS logs right now: a bunch of `TLS alert handshake_failure` with SNI mismatch summary. ALB target group tg-frontend-eu shows 4/6 unhealthy across ~30% of targets.

Kevin: any cert rotations pushed in the last 12h? I pushed a cert update to edge cert-store ~3h ago but it was supposed to be staged only. Checking commit history.

Sam (engops): quick check: DNS changes rolled earlier today — TTL was lowered to 60s for a canary, change batch ID C-2738. dig from multiple locations shows mixed A answers between old-edge and new-edge pools during propagation. Might be uneven rollout + cert mismatch on new hosts.

Nicole: customer-support receiving chat spikes reporting 502/524 from EU. I’ve flagged customers on EU region. Will update if we see any escalations.

Alex (on-call): running targeted checks:
```
# check ALB target health
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-frontend-eu/abcdef123
```
Output snippet:
```
{ "TargetHealthDescriptions": [ { "Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.45"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Description": "TLS handshake failed"}}, ... ] }
```

Alex (on-call): curl test to one of the unhealthy IPs yields TLS alert:
```
curl -v https://edge-eu.example.com/ -o /dev/null
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'edge-eu.example.com'
* Closing connection 0
```

Maya: that message looks like cert/SNI mismatch. Could be new hosts serving wrong cert (common name mismatch) or SNI not passed through at layer where traffic got routed.

Kevin: Confirmed — cert deployment job for stack-edge-eu had a mis-tag: the new cert is for `staging.edge.red` not `edge-eu.example.com`. I rolled a shadow cert earlier but didn't finish the swap. Rolling back now.

Jordan: while Kevin rolls cert, we should reduce exposure: start a staggered failover to eu-west-2 and add a temporary routing rule to divert new sessions. I can handle Route53 traffic policy change.

Sam (engops): propose steps (short):
1) Block new sessions to problem LB via ALB listener rule priority change (drain 30% of new connections).
2) Route 30% traffic to fallback region (eu-west-2) via weighted DNS change.
3) Re-deploy previous good cert to affected hosts and force ALB target health re-evaluation.
4) Monitor TLS error rate and target health; once stable, incrementally move traffic back.

Alex (on-call): executing step 1 -> updating ALB rule to lower priority and enable sticky draining.

IncidentBot: PagerDuty update -> PD-9283 acknowledged by Alex (on-call) at 6712348920. Escalation scheduled to Kevin in 6m if no update.

Kevin: rolling back cert now. running:
```
edge-certctl rollback --stack stack-edge-eu --cert-id cert-2026-04-prev
systemctl restart edge-proxy
```

Kevin: rollback applied. Restarted edge proxy on 12 hosts; triggering target health re-check.

Sam (engops): applying weighted DNS change (temporary):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZONE123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"edge-eu.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-2-fallback","Weight":30,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"34.200.11.22"}]}}]}'
```
Change submitted C-2742.

Nicole: support: some customers are already switched to fallback and reporting normal behavior. Good sign.

Maya: metrics update: TLS handshake error rate dropping from 5.2% -> 0.9% over last 5m. ALB target health: unhealthy count down to 1/30.

Jordan: good. Keep traffic routed and watch for error re-introduction before full rollback. Also capture any clients that might cache old DNS entries.

Alex (on-call): manual health probe loop running; will wait for stable 10m before removing weighted change.

IncidentBot: PagerDuty note -> PD-9283 escalation canceled (acknowledged). Notifying on-call that mitigation in progress.

Kevin: root cause preliminary: cert rollout automation mis-tagged cert, caused new hosts to serve incorrect CN. Combined with low TTL DNS canary probing caused some clients to hit mixed host set, increasing SNI mismatch symptoms.

Sam (engops): follow-up actions I’ve scheduled:
- Backfill cert deployment testing and add pre-deploy SNI validation (ticket OPS-1120).
- Revert low TTL on that record to standard 300s after rollout completes.
- Add Route53 health-check-based failover to reduce manual weighted changes.

Maya: metrics now stable for 12m. TLS errors at baseline, ALB healthy targets 30/30.

Alex (on-call): shifting traffic back incrementally (removing weighted fallback). Change C-2742 applied to remove eu-west-2 weight.

Nicole: customers updated; no major escalations.

Jordan: logging a follow-up incident for RCA and owners assigned: Kevin (cert automation), Sam (DNS policies), Maya (monitoring & alarms).

Alex (on-call): closing out this page for now. Will file a postmortem and link the incident timeline. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: PagerDuty incident PD-9283 marked resolved at 6712348965.

Alex (on-call): postmortem ticket: INC-2026-043 opened. Will include exact timeline, commands run, and mitigations.

Maya: adding note — recommend adding an automated smoke test that does an end-to-end TLS check right after any cert rollout (SNI, CN, and handshake success), to catch this earlier.

Kevin: agreed. I'll follow up on OPS-1120.

Nicole: closing support notify loop.

-- end of thread --
